title: Option to enable pipewire-virtual-surround-sound feature
line: Sound settings can now add a Virtual Surround Sound output that plays 5.1 and 7.1 audio as surround on headphones.
explanation: PipeWire can turn multichannel audio into headphone surround with a filter-chain sink, but it only ships example configs that the user has to copy and edit by hand, and plasma-pa had no PipeWire-side settings at all (its Configure menu was hidden on PipeWire). The change adds a checkable "Add virtual output device for surround sound on headphones" entry to the Sound page's Configure menu on PipeWire. Enabling it writes ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/plasma-pa-virtual-surround.conf (a 7.1 sofa spatializer graph using libmysofa's default.sofa HRTF, mixed to stereo) and restarts PipeWire, the same way Rename Devices applies its WirePlumber config; disabling removes the file and restarts again.

commits.message:
kcm: add an option for virtual surround sound on PipeWire

PipeWire can render 5.1 and 7.1 audio as surround sound on headphones,
but there was no way to enable it from Plasma. Add a Configure menu
entry that sets up its spatializer filter with the system's HRTF data.

BUG: 527041

media.caption: Master on PipeWire: no Configure menu, no way to enable virtual surround
Configure menu now offers the virtual surround output (PulseAudio-only entries stay hidden on PipeWire)
After enabling it, a "Virtual Surround Sound" output appears and can be made the default
